name: Vilnius University
summary: Founded 1579; more than 30 bachelor's and integrated programmes taught in English, in Vilnius, Kaunas and Šiauliai.

ib.text: Admitted on the grades in your IB results (upload diploma and transcript). Many programmes add a motivation letter, interview or video task; Medicine and Dentistry waive the exam with HL Biology 5 and Chemistry 5.

lastYear.text: EU/EFTA apply by 1 July; non-EU by 1 May

programmes.name: Business and Finance
programmes.about: Real business cases, an entrepreneurial approach and sustainable business creation and management, in modules of three courses a semester. Has ACBSP (USA) accreditation.
programmes.overview: Each semester is split into three modules, and teaching is built around real business challenges set by business experts rather than lectures alone. The emphasis falls on corporate finance: analysing cash flows, assessing investments, preparing budgets, choosing financing models, judging a company's financial position and its risks, and drafting development plans that secure funding. Graduates work as financial, investment, budget, treasury or risk analysts, accountants, banking officers and internal auditors in companies, banks, insurers, audit and consulting firms and the public sector, or start businesses.
programmes.selectionNote: Needs a 70% overall average; motivation is judged on recorded video answers and a possible remote interview.
programmes.ib: Overall grade average of at least 70%; a recorded video interview is part of the application.

programmes.name: International Business
programmes.about: Business studied through real challenges, teamwork and entrepreneurship, covering management, marketing and finance in an international setting. Has ACBSP (USA) accreditation.
programmes.overview: Each semester is split into three modules, and the subjects span marketing and sales, organisation and personnel management, accounting and finance, entrepreneurship, leadership, client relations, negotiation, business psychology, international protocol and economic analysis, plus setting up and winding up a company. Teaching is built around real business challenges, with project preparation, business communication and foreign languages alongside. Graduates work as international business, business development or operations managers, management consultants, project managers and trade specialists in finance, insurance, trade and marketing, and many start their own ventures.
programmes.selectionNote: Needs a 70% overall average; motivation is judged on recorded video answers and a possible remote interview.
programmes.ib: Overall grade average of at least 70%; a recorded video interview is part of the application.

programmes.name: Accounting and Audit
programmes.about: Trains accountants and auditors: accounting, taxes, audit procedures and analysing company performance, with practice supported by major audit and consulting firms.
programmes.overview: The first years cover business mathematics, economic theory, fundamentals of accounting, financial accounting, management, statistics and marketing, then cost accounting, corporate finance, business law, tax accounting, financial statements and management audit. Later courses turn to financial audit, budgeting, public-sector accounting, accounting information systems and performance evaluation, with course work, a professional practice and a bachelor thesis. Paid internships with large firms such as PwC, EY, Deloitte and KPMG are common, and studies can be combined with work. Graduates become accountants, auditors, financial analysts and consultants, or continue to a master's.
programmes.selectionNote: Needs a 60% overall average and one reference; strong applications are invited to an interview with the admissions committee.
programmes.ib: Overall grade average of at least 60% and one reference letter.

programmes.name: Economics and Finance
programmes.about: Economics, finance and data analysis, with statistics labs and a Bloomberg terminal, and an introduction to fintech products and their regulation.
programmes.overview: The degree rests on economics, finance and data analysis: corporate and public finance, financial markets, macroeconomics, statistics, econometrics and data visualisation, plus fintech technologies and their regulation. Lectures and seminars build argument and presentation skills, computer laboratories use statistical software and a Bloomberg terminal for live market data, and almost every course brings in guest speakers from economics or finance. Graduates work in banks, investment management, financial analysis, fintech, consulting, ministries, central banks and research institutes, as finance analysts, investment managers or business consultants.
programmes.selectionNote: Needs a 60% overall average and one reference; strong applications are invited to an interview.
programmes.ib: Overall grade average of at least 60% and one reference letter.

programmes.name: Global Marketing
programmes.about: International advertising business, brand management and consumer behaviour, in a programme accredited for seven years by international experts in 2025.
programmes.overview: The curriculum moves from foundations in management and marketing to applications across business sectors, the integration of sales, management and marketing, international marketing, and market research methods, with a group of individually chosen studies. You work with quantitative data, build advertising campaigns for digital and traditional media, and use AI tools for audience segmentation and campaign optimisation. Around eighty companies host students for professional internships each year, among them Danske Bank, Teltonika, Wolt, IKEA and DHL. Graduates work as sales managers, marketing experts, business managers and business developers.
programmes.selectionNote: Needs a 60% overall average and one reference; strong applications are invited to an interview.
programmes.ib: Overall grade average of at least 60% and one reference letter.

programmes.name: Management
programmes.about: Prepares business managers: strategy, organisation, HR, marketing, market research and finance. A double-degree option exists with the University of Granada.
programmes.overview: You study strategic business development, organisational management, human resources, marketing and market research, accounting and financial management, and business negotiation. Lecturers use practical examples, and you can take part in integrated practical activities, including creating a start-up in the VU TechHub pre-accelerator. There are study branches, among them one on global business and analytics, and a double-degree route spends five to six semesters at the University of Granada in Spain, ending with degrees from both universities. Graduates work as sales managers, marketing experts, business managers or developers in business and the public sector, run their own businesses, or continue to a master's.
programmes.selectionNote: Needs a 60% overall average and one reference; strong applications are invited to an interview.
programmes.ib: Overall grade average of at least 60% and one reference letter.

programmes.name: Quantitative Economics
programmes.about: Three-year economics and finance degree built on mathematical and econometric modelling and data work, with a double-degree option at Jean Monnet University in Saint-Étienne.
programmes.overview: The three years run from core economic principles, mathematical methods and statistics to economic theory, econometrics and finance, with a capstone project and an internship in the final year. Teaching is delivered entirely in English by research-active faculty and leans on applied research with empirical evidence. A double-degree option with the Saint-Etienne School of Economics at Jean Monnet University in France is available. Graduates work as financial analysts, data analysts, economists and research analysts in financial services, research institutions, government and consulting, and the English-language degree supports applications to master's programmes abroad.
programmes.selectionNote: Maths and English averages of at least 75%, a reference and an interview. The LAMA BPO route adds an entrance exam.
programmes.ib: Maths and English grade averages of at least 75% (7.5 of 10); one reference letter.

needs.note: Average of at least 75% (7.5 of 10) in maths
Average of at least 75% in English

programmes.name: Bioinformatics
programmes.about: Computer science joined to biology: analysing biological data and building computational methods, for research and high-tech industry.
programmes.overview: Mathematics, computer science and the life sciences are taught side by side, with teachers from the Faculty of Mathematics and Informatics, the Life Sciences Center and research institutes. Early semesters cover biology, chemistry, discrete mathematics, programming and biochemistry; later ones cover genetics, molecular and cell biology, algorithms, statistics, databases, software engineering and several courses in bioinformatics itself. Laboratory and programming practicals run throughout, with project work and a final internship and bachelor thesis. Graduates work as bioinformatics software specialists in research laboratories, biotechnology and pharmaceutical companies and genetic research, or continue to a master's or doctorate.
programmes.selectionNote: Maths and English averages of at least 7.5 out of 10, plus a remote motivational interview for everyone.
programmes.ib: Maths and English grade averages of at least 7.5 out of 10; everyone has a remote interview.

programmes.name: Business Data Analytics
programmes.about: Three-year programme in statistics, machine learning, business and finance: collecting, analysing and explaining complex data for decisions.
programmes.overview: Over three years you combine statistics and machine learning with business management, economics and finance, learning to collect, analyse and interpret complex data and to frame business problems in mathematical and statistical terms. You build business data analytics projects with specialised software, applying theory to real problem-solving. The programme collaborates with VU Business School and the University of Minho's School of Economics, Management and Political Science. Graduates work as business, financial and economic data analysts, forecasters, customer behaviour analysts and builders of recommendation systems, in consulting, finance and research.
programmes.selectionNote: Ranked on your school grades and motivation letter; no extra minimum is listed on the page.

programmes.name: Innovative Communication and Entrepreneurship
programmes.about: New programme joining communication and entrepreneurship: innovation, business models, digital content, audience analysis, with an internship and thesis.
programmes.overview: The degree starts with core academic skills, entrepreneurship and networking technologies, moves to innovation and business model development, integrated communication and audience analysis, and ends with research methods, digital content creation, leadership and sustainable business development. Teaching is practical, with real projects and business tasks, an internship and a final thesis applied to an actual setting, in cooperation with outside organisations. Graduates work as communications specialists, digital content creators, brand managers, public relations and marketing specialists, innovation project managers or start-up founders, in agencies, start-ups, public institutions and international organisations.
programmes.selectionNote: Needs a 70% overall average and a motivation letter; everyone who meets the formal requirements gets an interview.
programmes.ib: Overall grade average of at least 70% and a motivation letter; everyone is interviewed.

programmes.name: Chemistry of Nanomaterials
programmes.about: Making and studying nanostructured materials: theory plus laboratory work in synthesis and characterisation of nanomaterials.
programmes.overview: You begin with general chemistry, mathematics and physics, then analytical, physical, organic, inorganic and polymer chemistry, followed by biochemistry, quantum and colloid chemistry, spectroscopy and specialised nanochemistry subjects, with electives for deeper focus. Laboratory work and practical training are central, teaching you to make and analyse nanomaterials with modern instrumental methods and to work safely and in teams. Graduates work as materials and nanomaterials researchers, pharmaceutical nanotechnology researchers and quality control specialists in medicine, electronics, energy and environmental fields, or continue to a master's or doctorate.
programmes.selectionNote: Chemistry and maths averages of at least 60%, then an interview covering motivation, chemistry and English.
programmes.ib: Chemistry and maths grade averages of at least 60%; a motivational interview tests chemistry and English.

needs.note: Average of at least 60% in chemistry
Average of at least 60% in maths

programmes.name: Light Engineering
programmes.about: Practice-oriented study of lasers and light technology, with physics, chemistry, electronics and maths, and lab work on growth and characterisation equipment.
programmes.overview: The programme covers laser and semiconductor physics, optics, optoelectronics, digital modelling and smart lighting, on top of physics, chemistry, electronics and mathematics, including material synthesis, characterisation techniques and the principles of photovoltaic devices. Laboratory work on the university's growth and characterisation equipment is central, and students are encouraged to join research projects early. You can specialise deeply in an optoelectronics field or keep a broader base. Graduates work in light technology companies, with laser specialists and in research centres, helped by the strong Lithuanian laser industry, or continue to a master's or doctorate in laser physics, optics or materials science.
programmes.selectionNote: Physics and maths grades of at least 55%; a negative motivational interview means no place.
programmes.ib: Physics and maths grades of at least 55% of the maximum; a motivational interview decides.

needs.note: At least 55% of the maximum grade
At least 55% of the maximum grade

programmes.name: Politics of Global Challenges
programmes.about: Policy for global problems: pandemics, migration, climate, technology and inequality, preparing people who can bring politicians, business and NGOs together.
programmes.overview: Political science theory sits beside social sciences, humanities and the science behind global problems in technology, environment and health, with qualitative, quantitative and digital research methods, big data analysis and data visualisation. Teaching is research-oriented: you formulate a research problem tied to a global challenge, plan it and carry out small-scale scientific or applied research, often working with people from other disciplines. Graduates work as policy analysts, strategic planning specialists, government analysts, programme officers in NGOs and international organisations, or climate policy specialists, or continue to a master's in social sciences, humanities or interdisciplinary studies.
programmes.selectionNote: Ranked on school grades plus an assessment of motivation.

programmes.name: Sustainability and Future Societies
programmes.about: Social sustainability and change, drawing on sociology, social work, psychology, criminology, management, technology and AI.
programmes.overview: You apply sociology, social work, psychology, criminology, management, technology and AI to social sustainability problems, with advanced social research methods, demographic research, policy evaluation and project management for social innovation. Learning is applied, through project work, research and community-based initiatives, and working with communities, organisations and international partners. Graduates work as urban planners, sustainability officers and policy analysts in the public sector, as social innovation managers and impact assessors in NGOs, or as sustainability consultants and corporate responsibility leads in business.
programmes.selectionNote: Ranked on school grades; motivated applicants are invited to an interview with the admissions committee.

programmes.name: English Philology
programmes.about: English linguistics, literature and the cultures of English-speaking countries, with language work towards C1-C2 and a minor from another programme.
programmes.overview: You study how English is structured and used in society and culture, the literature of English-speaking countries and media analysis, while building communication skills at C1-C2 level through academic writing, creative and content writing, public speaking and translation. Digital resources support independent and group work, and you can add a minor in German philology, Spanish language and literature, or Scandinavian studies. Graduates work as teachers, translators, editors, publishers, journalists, content creators and business communication specialists in education, media and cultural institutions, or continue to a master's at home or abroad.
programmes.selectionNote: Ranked on school grades; those who qualify get a motivational interview. A state-funded place is applied for through LAMA BPO.

programmes.name: English and Another Foreign Language
programmes.about: English plus a second language (here German), with intercultural skills and the culture, society and politics of both language areas.
programmes.overview: You study English to C1 level and German to B2, with a focus on the structure of both languages and how linguistic phenomena relate, alongside language and literature, knowledge of the ancient world and specialised modules, plus electives chosen to your interests. Teaching stresses practical, real-life language use across fields and builds teamwork, critical thinking and self-assessment. Graduates work in translation, interpreting, publishing, content creation, language teaching and customer service, in foreign institutions in Lithuania, embassies, international organisations, media and business, or continue to a master's.
programmes.selectionNote: Ranked on school grades; those who qualify get a motivational interview. A state-funded place is applied for through LAMA BPO.

programmes.name: English and Another Foreign Language
programmes.about: English plus a second language (here French), with intercultural skills and the culture, society and politics of both language areas.
programmes.overview: You study English to C1 level and French to B2, with a focus on the structure of both languages and how linguistic phenomena relate, alongside language and literature, knowledge of the ancient world and specialised modules, plus electives chosen to your interests. Teaching stresses practical, real-life language use across fields and builds teamwork, critical thinking and self-assessment. Graduates work in translation, interpreting, publishing, content creation, language teaching and customer service, in foreign institutions in Lithuania, embassies, international organisations, media, finance and logistics, or continue to a master's.
programmes.selectionNote: Ranked on school grades; those who qualify get a motivational interview. A state-funded place is applied for through LAMA BPO.

programmes.name: English and Another Foreign Language
programmes.about: English plus a second language (here Spanish), with intercultural skills and the culture, society and politics of both language areas.
programmes.overview: You study English to C1 level and Spanish to B2, with a focus on the structure of both languages and how linguistic phenomena relate, alongside language and literature, knowledge of the ancient world and specialised modules. Learning options include semester exchanges through Erasmus+ at Spanish universities, internships built into the curriculum, and elective modules for a personal path. Graduates work as translators, interpreters, language specialists, content creators and teachers in embassies, international organisations, cultural institutions, media, publishing, finance and logistics, or freelance, or continue to a master's.
programmes.selectionNote: Ranked on school grades; those who qualify get a motivational interview. A state-funded place is applied for through LAMA BPO.

programmes.name: Spanish Philology
programmes.about: Spanish to professional level plus the history, literature and culture of Spain and Latin America, with modern methods of language and literature research.
programmes.overview: You learn Spanish to a professional level (C1-C2) and analyse the language through phonetics, grammar, lexicology, pragmatics and language development, while studying the literature and cultures of Spain and Latin America with current methods of language and literature research. Optional topics include Spanish women's literature, Spanish art, contemporary theatre and the history of Spanish-speaking America. Graduates work as Spanish teachers, translators, interpreters, journalists, content creators and marketing or tourism professionals, in government, international organisations and embassies, or continue to a master's in arts, humanities or social sciences.
programmes.selectionNote: Ranked on school grades; those who qualify get a motivational interview. A state-funded place is applied for through LAMA BPO.

programmes.name: Lithuanian Studies
programmes.about: Learn Lithuanian to B2 while studying Lithuanian culture, literature, history, politics and the neighbouring Baltic countries.
programmes.overview: You learn or improve Lithuanian to B2 level while studying Lithuanian culture, literature, history, and social and political life, with a look at the neighbouring Baltic countries. The degree develops research methods in linguistics and cultural studies, project skills and cross-cultural analysis, and can be combined with other fields such as management, communication or pedagogy for a personal path. Graduates work as language teachers, curriculum developers, cultural project managers, museum specialists, translators and policy analysts wherever intercultural competence and knowledge of Lithuania are needed.
programmes.selectionNote: Ranked on school grades; those who qualify get a motivational interview. A state-funded place is applied for through LAMA BPO.
programmes.ib: Taught in English for the first two years and in Lithuanian after that, per the national programme list; no Lithuanian needed to start.

programmes.name: Multilingualism and Digital Technologies
programmes.about: New programme joining English and German language and culture with applied informatics, for work on multilingual digital content and tools.
programmes.overview: You study English (up to C1-C2) and German (to B2) with comparative linguistics and the literature and cultures of both, alongside applied informatics: digital content creation, data management, web technologies, and language technology including natural language processing. The programme moves from foundations to more complex subjects and asks you to design digital solutions that suit their target audience, using modern IT and AI-based tools and working in multilingual teams. Graduates work as digital communication, language technology, localisation, web content and digital transformation specialists, or as junior software developers and project coordinators.
programmes.selectionNote: Ranked on school grades; those who qualify get a motivational interview. A state-funded place is applied for through LAMA BPO.
programmes.ib: German studies start from the beginning; English at B2 is the minimum.

programmes.name: Central and East European Languages and Cultures
programmes.about: Languages and cultures of the region with a Polish Studies focus: Polish-Lithuanian history, the Vilnius region and contemporary border culture; taught in English.
programmes.overview: This Polish Studies route is designed for beginners, taking you from first steps to advanced Polish alongside Polish literature and culture, the history of Central and Eastern Europe and modern methods of linguistic research. The coursework links language with analytical thinking and intercultural awareness for use in diplomacy, cultural mediation and international communication. Graduates work as international relations specialists, Polish teachers, editors and proofreaders, cultural project managers, researchers and freelance translators, in embassies, international organisations, cultural institutions, media and publishing.
programmes.selectionNote: Ranked on school grades; those who qualify get a motivational interview. A state-funded place is applied for through LAMA BPO.
programmes.ib: Needs Polish and English at B1 or better, shown by certificate; English at B2 is the minimum for the taught-in-English list.

family.name: Central and East European Languages and Cultures

programmes.name: Central and East European Languages and Cultures
programmes.about: Languages and cultures of the region with a Russian Studies focus, taught in English.
programmes.overview: This Russian Studies route is designed for beginners and takes Russian to B2-C1 level alongside literature, cultural theory and linguistic analysis, set in the wider region with attention to its politics, history and media literacy. The structure is flexible: you can choose courses from politics, history, management or pedagogy, and study more than twenty languages. Teaching builds independent research and text analysis across styles and genres. Graduates work as international relations specialists, language educators, translators, editors, cultural project managers and researchers in media, publishing, diplomacy, government and international organisations, or continue to further study.
programmes.selectionNote: Ranked on school grades; those who qualify get a motivational interview. A state-funded place is applied for through LAMA BPO.

family.name: Central and East European Languages and Cultures

programmes.name: Scandinavian Studies
programmes.about: Nordic languages, history, welfare model and culture, with one language (here Danish) taken to B2; about half the curriculum is shaped by your own choices.
programmes.overview: You take Danish from the ground up to B2 level while studying the Nordic region more broadly: its welfare model, historical turning points, Viking-era heritage, mythology, media and popular culture, with options on endangered Nordic languages and cultures, Nordic music and the multicultural urban identities of young people. Learning is experience-based, and nearly half the curriculum is shaped by your own choices, including courses from other programmes. Graduates work as translators, interpreters, teachers, cultural specialists, researchers and media professionals, in embassies, international organisations and Nordic companies, or continue to humanities or social science master's study.
programmes.selectionNote: Ranked on school grades; those who qualify get a motivational interview. A state-funded place is applied for through LAMA BPO.

programmes.name: Scandinavian Studies
programmes.about: Nordic languages, history, welfare model and culture, with one language (here Norwegian) taken to B2; about half the curriculum is shaped by your own choices.
programmes.overview: You take Norwegian from the ground up to B2 level while studying the Nordic region more broadly: its welfare model, historical turning points, Viking-era heritage, mythology, media and popular culture, with options on endangered Nordic languages and cultures, Nordic music and the multicultural urban identities of young people. Learning is experience-based, and nearly half the curriculum is shaped by your own choices. Graduates work as translators, interpreters, lecturers, teachers, cultural specialists, researchers, tourism specialists and media professionals, in embassies, international organisations and Nordic companies.
programmes.selectionNote: Ranked on school grades; those who qualify get a motivational interview. A state-funded place is applied for through LAMA BPO.

programmes.name: Scandinavian Studies
programmes.about: Nordic languages, history, welfare model and culture, with one language (here Swedish) taken to B2; about half the curriculum is shaped by your own choices.
programmes.overview: You take Swedish from the ground up to B2 level while studying the Nordic region more broadly: its welfare model, historical turning points, Viking-era heritage, mythology, media and popular culture, with options on endangered Nordic languages and cultures, Nordic music and the multicultural urban identities of young people. Shared humanities courses sit beside Scandinavian ones, and nearly half the curriculum is shaped by your own choices. Graduates work as translators, interpreters, teachers, cultural specialists, researchers, tourism specialists and media professionals, in embassies, international organisations and Nordic companies, and many go on to advanced humanities study.
programmes.selectionNote: Ranked on school grades; those who qualify get a motivational interview. A state-funded place is applied for through LAMA BPO.

programmes.name: Scandinavian Studies
programmes.about: Nordic languages, history, welfare model and culture, with one language (here Finnish) taken to B2; about half the curriculum is shaped by your own choices.
programmes.overview: You take Finnish from the ground up to B2 level while studying the Nordic region more broadly: its welfare model, historical turning points, Viking-era heritage, mythology, media and popular culture, with options on endangered Nordic languages and cultures, Nordic music and the multicultural urban identities of young people. Learning is experience-based, and nearly half the curriculum is shaped by your own choices, including courses from other programmes. Graduates work as translators, interpreters, teachers, lecturers, cultural specialists, researchers and tourism or media professionals, in embassies, international organisations and Nordic companies, or continue to humanities or social science study.
programmes.selectionNote: Ranked on school grades; those who qualify get a motivational interview. A state-funded place is applied for through LAMA BPO.

programmes.name: Nursing
programmes.about: Nursing science and practice leading to a bachelor's degree and the qualification of a general practice nurse, with leadership and teamwork skills.
programmes.overview: Lectures and seminars use clinical examples, case studies and problem-solving exercises, and clinical placements across all levels of the health service take you from observation to increasingly complex procedures under qualified supervision. You build skills in communication, ethics, health promotion, disease prevention, work organisation, leadership and medical information systems, and can take part in research at university clinics within interdisciplinary teams. Graduates work as general practice nurses in hospitals, outpatient and family practice, rehabilitation and long-term care, or independently under Lithuanian law, and can continue to a master's in Lithuania or abroad.
programmes.selectionNote: Biology, English and one of chemistry, physics or maths are required, plus a motivational interview.
programmes.ib: Biology, English and one of chemistry, physics or maths are required; there is a motivational interview.

programmes.name: Medicine
programmes.about: Six-year integrated degree producing doctors, with the sciences medicine rests on and clinical training; English-taught and fee-paying for every applicant.
programmes.overview: The degree builds the sciences medicine rests on, including human anatomy, physiology and pathology and scientific methodology, then moves into clinical disciplines, with practice in history-taking, physical examination, laboratory work, instrumental investigations and treatment planning. Clinical placements fill a large share of the later years, and students can take part in research and international exchange. Students who do not speak Lithuanian receive Lithuanian language teaching over six semesters, aimed at the level needed in clinical settings. Graduates go into residency and specialisation, hospital practice, public health, research or industry, and the degree supports mobility across Europe.
programmes.selectionNote: Online entrance exam (€200) unless you hold HL Biology 5 and HL Chemistry 5; a motivation essay is also part of the application. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.
programmes.ib: Online entrance exam, waived with IB HL Biology 5 and HL Chemistry 5; Biology at school is required.

needs.note: Exam waived with HL Biology 5 and HL Chemistry 5

programmes.name: Dentistry
programmes.about: Five-year integrated degree for dentists, with theory and practice built to European Directive 2005/36/EC requirements.
programmes.overview: You start with anatomy, physiology and biochemistry and move gradually into pre-clinical practice with simulated procedures, then into clinical placements where diagnostic, therapeutic and preventive dental work is done under supervision. Clinical intensity grows each year, and in the final semesters you manage your own patients from diagnosis to treatment planning. The curriculum follows EU standards for the profession and stresses professional ethics, communication and teamwork with other health professionals. Graduates work in private or public dental practice, set up their own practices, enter residency in fields such as orthodontics or oral surgery, or go into research, academia or industry.
programmes.selectionNote: Online entrance exam (€200) unless you hold HL Biology 5 and HL Chemistry 5; a motivation essay is also part of the application. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.
programmes.ib: Online entrance exam, waived with IB HL Biology 5 and HL Chemistry 5; Biology at school is required.

needs.note: Exam waived with HL Biology 5 and HL Chemistry 5

programmes.name: Economics and Management
programmes.about: Economics joined to management, entrepreneurship and risk management, for forecasting market change and building sustainable business ideas; taught in Kaunas.
programmes.overview: You study economics, finance and financial management, marketing and consumer behaviour, statistics and econometrics, international economics, business analytics and risk management, plus themes such as the digital, environmental, urban and sharing economies. Teaching centres on data analysis and decision-making in management, investment and business financing, with independent learning, an internship and a bachelor thesis, and Erasmus exchange is possible. Graduates work as economists, project managers, finance specialists, business analysts, consultants or civil servants, in industrial and logistics companies and government agencies, or start their own ventures.
programmes.selectionNote: Ranked on school grades; Kaunas Faculty may invite you to a remote interview, and pupils without national exams sit an entrance test.
programmes.ib: Kaunas Faculty may interview you remotely; applicants without national university entrance exams sit an entrance exam.

programmes.name: Information Systems and Cyber Security
programmes.about: Secure information systems: programming, networks, ethical hacking, cryptography and digital crime investigation, finishing with an internship and thesis; taught in Kaunas.
programmes.overview: You learn programming, algorithms, databases and computer networks together with their security side, then operating systems, information security, ethical hacking, cryptography, digital crime investigation, virtualisation, AI fundamentals and cyber law. About half of the subjects are taught by practitioners, and you work on real information system development, testing and risk management, finishing with an internship and a thesis. Electives let you take AI and automation courses from any programme at the university. Graduates work as security specialists, analysts, architects, programmers, testers, database administrators and project managers, or in auditing and security management.
programmes.selectionNote: Ranked on school grades; Kaunas Faculty may invite you to a remote interview, and pupils without national exams sit an entrance test.
programmes.ib: Kaunas Faculty may interview you remotely; applicants without national university entrance exams sit an entrance exam.

programmes.name: Language and Artificial Intelligence Management
programmes.about: English linguistics joined to information systems, for analysing and managing how generative AI and human language interact; taught in Kaunas.
programmes.overview: The degree joins English linguistics with information systems: semantics, pragmatics and discourse analysis, the analysis of natural and AI-generated language, writing and refining queries for generative AI, programming and data processing basics, how training data is built and checked, and the ethical and legal principles of AI-generated language. You learn to design, assess and improve how people interact with generative AI, to spot bias, manipulation and disinformation, and to reach C1 English. Graduates work as human-AI interaction specialists, content quality or discourse analysts, conversational systems and disinformation specialists, or AI policy specialists.
programmes.selectionNote: Ranked on school grades; those who qualify get a motivational interview.

programmes.name: Marketing Technologies
programmes.about: Smart digital advertising, consumer communication environments and analytics, mixing marketing with information technology; taught in Kaunas.
programmes.overview: You combine traditional and digital marketing theory with information technology: e-marketing strategy, beginner-level programming, AI applications, mobile app development, data analytics and the digitisation of business models. Theory is paired with practice on real situations, including collecting, analysing and presenting marketing research data and hands-on work with AI tools, and Erasmus exchange is available. Graduates work as internet marketing and marketing technology specialists, website developers, information systems analysts, product and project managers, content managers and social media or PPC managers.
programmes.selectionNote: Ranked on school grades; Kaunas Faculty may invite you to a remote interview, and pupils without national exams sit an entrance test.
programmes.ib: Kaunas Faculty may interview you remotely; applicants without national university entrance exams sit an entrance exam.

programmes.name: Economics and Investment
programmes.about: Economics with mathematics, management, finance, law and accounting, for analysing companies and economies; taught at Šiauliai Academy.
programmes.overview: The degree gives a broad base in economics, mathematics, management, finance, law, marketing and accounting, then two elective blocks, one in finance and investments and one in global economy. You learn to analyse economic situations at company, national and global level, assess resource use and company performance, support funding and investment decisions and take part in macroeconomic policy planning. Graduates work as economists, financial analysts and managers in public and private organisations, banks and businesses, forecasting economic indicators.
programmes.selectionNote: Ranked on school grades; strong applications are invited to an interview with the admissions committee.

programmes.name: Software Engineering
programmes.about: Software development, testing and secure management: programming technologies, architecture, networks, databases and algorithms; taught at Šiauliai Academy.
programmes.overview: Following ACM guidelines, the degree joins software engineering with computer science: programming languages and frameworks, algorithms and data structures, databases, computer architecture, networks and operating systems, and the whole development lifecycle from requirements and design to testing and quality assurance. You choose between two branches, e-service systems for banks, insurers and the public sector, or robotic systems, covering robotic architectures and control software. Graduates work as systems analysts, architects, software developers, automation engineers, database administrators and testers in software firms and e-services, or continue to a master's.
programmes.selectionNote: Ranked on school grades; strong applications are invited to an interview with the admissions committee.

notes: An EU citizen has two routes: pay the fee via apply.vu.lt (€3,250 to €6,000 a year, Medicine €14,100, Dentistry €15,000), or apply through LAMA BPO for a state-funded place; Medicine and Dentistry are fee-paying only.
The LAMA BPO competitive score weights four school subjects 0.4, 0.2, 0.2 and 0.2; IB holders upload their diploma and the SKVC recognition decision instead of converting grades.
The application fee is €100 and covers up to three programmes; English is shown by a test (IELTS 6.5 and equivalents) unless English was your language of instruction.
